ops.catering: Outside food and drink may not be brought into the building for food hygiene reasons, and food and drink service is limited to designated companies (bringing food or drink into the seating areas of Hall A and Hall C, and cooking there, is also prohibited). Catering is delivered directly from the central kitchen in the building; options include party menus, boxed meals, breakfast/lunch/dinner, and light meals and drinks, and there are limited menus for conference rooms used on their own. The catering service application form must be submitted 2 weeks in advance. Hall E has electrical and water supply/drainage pits, so exhibits involving cooking or food and drink are also possible, but the Tokyo International Forum rules on bringing in food and drink and the guidance of the Chiyoda Public Health Center must be followed. (Source: Facility Usage Guide, as of September 2025; Documents to Submit After Booking)
ops.restaurants: In the building there is Toutenkou (Chinese) on the 7th floor of the Glass Building, and Sizzler, Saigon (Vietnamese), Papa Milano (Italian), Sakagura Restaurant Takara and Pronto on the 1st basement floor; all offer party menus. There are also Hama-zushi on the 1st floor, cafes, FamilyMart and others. In the Glass Building conference rooms, a private-room buffet party plan by a chef from the Imperial Hotel (free drinks, room fee, tax and service charge included) is also available. (Source: Official website, Shops & Restaurants, retrieved October 2026)
ops.prevDaySetup: Hours of use run from entry to exit, including setup and teardown. Basic hours of use are 9:00-23:00 for Hall A, 9:00-22:00 for Halls B7, B5, C, D7, D5, D1 and E, and 9:00-21:00 for conference rooms (extensions in 1-hour units; late-night and early-morning use by prior consultation). When a hall is used on a day other than the event day only for setup, teardown or rehearsal, a dedicated "setup, teardown and rehearsal" rate applies (examples: Hall A weekdays, full day: 2,484,240 yen [event rate: 4,140,400 yen]; Hall B7 weekdays, full day: 1,201,200 yen [event rate: 2,002,000 yen]; tax included). Setup, teardown and rehearsal on the event day itself are charged at the event rate, and air conditioning in Hall E is charged separately only on setup/teardown days (cooling 35,200 yen/hour, heating 27,500 yen/hour). (Source: Facility Usage Guide, as of September 2025; Capacity and Rental Fee List PDF)
ops.waitingRooms: Hall A has dressing rooms, waiting rooms and a VIP waiting room, and the fees for ancillary facilities such as dressing rooms and waiting rooms are included in the hall rental fee (Hall C also has dressing rooms and waiting rooms, likewise included in the rental fee). Halls B7, B5, D7 and D1 also have waiting rooms (B7 and D7 have dressing rooms and waiting rooms); Hall D7 has 6 dressing rooms and waiting rooms on the same floor, and Hall D5 can use the 2 meeting rooms connected to its lobby as waiting rooms as well. Hall E has an organizer's waiting room, and among the Glass Building conference rooms only G701 comes with a dedicated waiting room (22.6 m²).
ops.loadingHours: The building is open 7:00-23:30. After closing and before opening (23:30 to 7:00 the next day), use the night entrance on the 1st floor, and event staff wear a "staff badge". Delivery vehicles enter from the "general parking and loading area entrance" on the 1st floor of the Glass Building on the JR Yurakucho Station side, split from general vehicles (which continue to the 3rd basement floor) on the 2nd basement floor, and proceed to the dedicated space for each facility in the loading area on the 2nd basement floor. The "load-in and load-out plan" and the "load-in/load-out vehicle pass" must be submitted 1 week in advance, and the venue management plan for setup and teardown 10 days in advance. Hall D7 has a freight elevator. (Source: Loading Area, Parking Entrance and Staff Entrance page; Documents to Submit After Booking page)
ops.parking: The parking lot on the 3rd basement floor has 417 spaces for standard passenger cars (including 7 for people with disabilities, 2 EV rapid-charging only and 10 EV standard-charging priority) and 10 for motorcycles, open 7:00-23:30 (open every day of the year; no entry or exit outside these hours). It is for standard passenger cars up to 2.2 m high, 1.9 m wide and 5.4 m long; large buses, trucks and bicycles cannot park. The fee for standard passenger cars is 200 yen per 30 minutes (on weekdays there is a long-stay discount of 2,000 yen for more than 5 hours up to 10 hours), and for organizers 2-hour tickets (normally 800 yen) are sold at 700 yen each. (Source: Parking page; Event Support Services, Other Services, retrieved October 2026)
ops.vehicleRules: Vehicles cannot be left in the loading area; if a vehicle must be left, use the paid parking lot on the 3rd basement floor. A "load-in/load-out vehicle pass" is required to enter the loading area and must be displayed on the windshield. The loading space differs by facility used, so the "load-in and load-out plan" must be submitted in advance. The general parking lot on the 3rd basement floor is only for standard passenger cars up to 2.2 m high, 1.9 m wide and 5.4 m long. Buses carrying participants use the bus drop-off area on the Tokyo Station side of the Glass Building, and a "bus drop-off area use notification" must be submitted 2 weeks in advance (consult the sales representative beforehand).
